4. // Flag projection helpers
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. // The seven flag projections shared with the sibling `pde` module (`spec_present_set`,
8. // `spec_rw_set`, `spec_us_set`, `spec_pwt_set`, `spec_pcd_set`, `spec_a_set`, `spec_d_set`) are
9. // reused from there to avoid duplicate definitions colliding through the `paging` glob re-export.

11.     spec_present_set,
12.     spec_rw_set,
13.     spec_us_set,
14.     spec_pwt_set,
15.     spec_pcd_set,
16.     spec_a_set,
17.     spec_d_set,
18. };
19. 
20. // The copy-on-write projection is PTE-specific (the PDE sibling has a page-size bit instead), so it
21. // is defined here. The enum is two-valued (`0` = clear, `1 << SHIFT` = set), isomorphic to `bool`.
22. pub open spec fn spec_cow_set(f: CopyOnWriteFlag) -> bool {
23.     f is CopyOnWrite
24. }
25. 
26. //==================================================================================================
27. // PageTableEntryFlags — abstract value (the eight control bits)
28. //==================================================================================================
29. 
30. // To a caller a flags bundle is exactly its eight paging-control bits. The bit-packing into the
31. // raw `PteWord` is hidden (the View is `closed`), realizing the encoding-independence the caller
32. // analysis demands. The single structural difference from the `pde` sibling is the OS-defined
33. // `cow` (copy-on-write, AVL) bit in place of the PDE's hardware `large_page` (PS) bit.
34. pub struct PteFlagsView {
35.     /// Present (P) bit — the entry maps a page (`is_present`).
36.     pub present: bool,
37.     /// Read/Write (R/W) bit — writes permitted (`is_writable`).
38.     pub writable: bool,
39.     /// User/Supervisor (U/S) bit — user-mode access permitted (`is_user`).
40.     pub user: bool,
41.     /// Page-Write-Through (PWT) bit.
42.     pub write_through: bool,
43.     /// Page-Cache-Disable (PCD) bit.
44.     pub cache_disabled: bool,
45.     /// Accessed (A) bit.
46.     pub accessed: bool,
47.     /// Dirty (D) bit.
48.     pub dirty: bool,
49.     /// Copy-on-write (OS-defined AVL) bit — set by `set_cow`, read by `is_cow`.
50.     pub cow: bool,
51. }
52. 
53. impl View for PageTableEntryFlags {
54.     type V = PteFlagsView;
55. 
56.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> PteFlagsView {
57.         PteFlagsView {
58.             present: spec_present_set(self.present),
59.             writable: spec_rw_set(self.read_write),
60.             user: spec_us_set(self.user_supervisor),
61.             write_through: spec_pwt_set(self.page_write_through),
62.             cache_disabled: spec_pcd_set(self.page_cache_disable),
63.             accessed: spec_a_set(self.accessed),
64.             dirty: spec_d_set(self.dirty),
65.             cow: spec_cow_set(self.cow),
66.         }
67.     }
68. }

72.     // value, so the invariant is vacuous. Kept explicit for uniformity.
73.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
74.         true
75.     }
76. }
77. 
78. // Abstract value produced by `PageTableEntryFlags::new`: records each of the seven argument bits
79. // faithfully and defaults the OS-defined copy-on-write bit to `false` (`NotCopyOnWrite`), since it
80. // is not a parameter (caller invariant: callers rely on `cow` defaulting to `NotCopyOnWrite`).
81. pub open spec fn spec_pte_flags_new(
82.     present: PresentFlag,
83.     read_write: ReadWriteFlag,
84.     user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag,
85.     page_write_through: PageWriteThroughFlag,
86.     page_cache_disable: PageCacheDisableFlag,
87.     accessed: AccessedFlag,
88.     dirty: DirtyFlag,
89. ) -> PteFlagsView {
90.     PteFlagsView {
91.         present: spec_present_set(present),
92.         writable: spec_rw_set(read_write),
93.         user: spec_us_set(user_supervisor),
94.         write_through: spec_pwt_set(page_write_through),
95.         cache_disabled: spec_pcd_set(page_cache_disable),
96.         accessed: spec_a_set(accessed),
97.         dirty: spec_d_set(dirty),
98.         cow: false,
99.     }
100. }
101. 
102. //==================================================================================================
103. // PageTableEntry — abstract value (flags + frame)
104. //==================================================================================================
105. 
106. // A PTE is the pair `(flags, frame)`. The frame is abstracted as its integer index (the
107. // `FrameNumber` View); the physical base address it yields is *derived* (`frame * FRAME_SIZE`),
108. // never stored.
109. pub struct PteView {
110.     /// The eight control bits this entry was built with.
111.     pub flags: PteFlagsView,
112.     /// The frame index this entry points at (== the inner `FrameNumber`'s `@`).
113.     pub frame: int,
114. }
115. 
116. impl View for PageTableEntry {
117.     type V = PteView;
118. 
119.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> PteView {
120.         PteView { flags: self.flags@, frame: self.frame@ }
121.     }
122. }
123.

125.     // The only real constraint is the frame bound, inherited verbatim from the `FrameNumber` type
126.     // invariant. It is what makes the (out-of-scope) `frame_address` total and overflow-free: the
127.     // derived physical base `frame * FRAME_SIZE` is well-defined and cannot overflow `usize`. (The
128.     // flags carry no cross-field constraint — `PageTableEntryFlags::inv` is vacuously `true` — so
129.     // they add nothing here.)
130.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
131.         0 <= self@.frame <= FrameNumber::spec_max()
132.     }
133. }
134.

136. // frame (caller invariant: constructor fidelity).
137. pub open spec fn spec_pte_new(flags: PteFlagsView, frame: int) -> PteView {
138.     PteView { flags, frame }

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `mm::virt::identity_map`

These three exec functions realize the V==P identity mapping through the page-table hardware
trust boundary. Each carries its **full** `#[verus_spec]` contract unchanged (no spec weakening);
the `external_body` only trusts the *body* until the `mm::virt` page-table permission ghost token
is realized. This is the same deferred-ghost-token class as `table::write`
(no contents `ensures`) and `kframe::new` (the caller already TCB-listed *because* it calls
`identity_map_page`). All three were verified-by-`admit()` in the spec phase; the `admit()` is now
replaced by the codebase-sanctioned `external_body` + this listing.

  `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR.alloc_as::<[PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH]>()`, whose contract carries
  `requires bump_view(self).inv()` (`src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:350`). `bump_view` is a
  parameter-free `uninterp spec fn` with **no** establishing lemma and **no** `type_invariant`
  anywhere in `src/libs/bump_allocator/` (verified: `grep -rn "bump_view" src` filtered to

  allocator's own deferred ghost token — it is **not** derivable from `ensure_pt`'s sole
  precondition `identity_map_view().inv()`, so the alloc-path obligation cannot be discharged
  in-body. Same cross-module deferral class as `kframe::new`. Contract preserved verbatim:
  `Ok(pt_paddr) => identity_map_view().inv() && spec_is_page_aligned(pt_paddr)`,
  `Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv()`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs::ensure_pte` — installs the leaf PTE via
  `Table::<PageTableEntry>::write`, which is deliberately **contents-free**
  (`external_body`, only `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, no contents `ensures`; a contents
  postcondition is documented-unsound — see the `table::write` entry above). There is therefore no
  spec link from a concrete PTE write to the parameter-free `identity_map_view().mapped`, so the
  `mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr))` postcondition is the deferred page-table permission
  token (the `identity_map_view()` `v -> v'` transition). Contract preserved verbatim:
  `Ok(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr))`,
  `Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && !...contains(...)`.

  to the parameter-free `identity_map_view()`, so the `accessible(phys_addr)` postcondition rests
  on the same `mm::virt` token. Note `kframe::new` is **already** TCB-listed precisely *because it
  calls this function* needing the unrealized token. Contract preserved verbatim:
  `Ok(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@)`,
  `Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && !...accessible(...)`.

  `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR`). Opaque external type, no fields modeled; listed for completeness so
